target_customer: Hardware designers and product makers who want thin, flexible, low-cost lit labels, indicators and displays
problem: Conventional OLED displays are expensive and rigid. Sinovia prints OLED layers roll to roll, like newspapers, to make paper-thin flexible emissive displays and lighting films.
business_model: Hardware component sales and custom printed film, plus government research grants
product_category: Printed flexible OLED displays and light films

founders.name: George Burkhard
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders began the work in 2009 during their PhD programs at Stanford.

founders.name: Whitney (surname not stated)
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the YC launch post per the YC page; surname not given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Roll-to-roll printing of OLED stacks requires materials science, barrier encapsulation and process control, a research-grade hardware problem for a seven person team.

defensibility.rationale: Process know-how and patents are plausible moats, but no patent count was verified. Incumbent display makers have deep resources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying found. Other printed OLED firms such as JOLED and Kateeva struggled or went bankrupt, which shows the sector is hard.

market_need_then: Interest in flexible displays for wearables and IoT was growing in 2016, and a US DOE SBIR project on roll-to-roll OLED lighting substrates ran from April 2018 to January 2019 (DOE page, not explicitly linked to Sinovia in the snippet).

branding.domain_note: Uses sinoviatech.com rather than an exact .com, suggesting sinovia.com was unavailable; not sourced.
branding.community_and_virality: Showed at Display Week 2023 I-Zone and launched a lit OLED label for a Spanish cava brand, covered by OLED-Info.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche trade press coverage only; no mascot, community or brand press found.

pivots.to: Printed Light Film, a flexible light source replacing LEDs, PCBs and optics
pivots.why: Not stated; the 2026 website emphasizes the film.

outcome_analysis: Sinovia is a Stanford spinout that printed OLED displays roll to roll and joined YC in W17. It is still active in San Carlos in 2026, showing products at Display Week 2023 and shipping a lit label, but it has stayed small and capital-light. Funding is only visible through unreliable aggregators, so the pace of growth and any scale outcome are unverified.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights says 13.7M over 11 rounds, thecompanycheck 10.68M over 8, ZoomInfo 150K over 1; the latest round 2.57M is dated 2023-07 or 2023-01 with conflicting labels. No primary release found, so no round is recorded. A DOE SBIR of 150K (2018) is shown by a DOE page but not tied to Sinovia in the text I saw. The eenewseurope article returned by search was about JOLED, not Sinovia. YC page says founded 2010; CB Insights 2011. Competitors empty: nothing dated near 2017 found. Completeness pass: the $2.57M raise dated 2023-07-12 from a $5M offering is now recorded from Fundz alone (labeled seed there; CB Insights leaves the type blank). CB Insights reports $13.7M over 11 rounds in total, so most rounds are still missing. Form D not seen.
